battle.name: 維京人第二次突襲葡萄牙
battle.theater: 阿爾加維與聖文森特海角
battle.brief: 966年，一支北歐長船隊再度南下，在今葡萄牙阿爾加維一帶登岸掠掠，隨後於聖文森特海角與科爾多瓦埃米爾國及北方基督教諸侯的聯軍交戰遭敗。戰爭的關鍵全在近身：登陸的維京戰士與聯軍步兵在盾牆後互相刺突，羅馬短劍代表的正是這套以刺為主、靠盾配合的近戰邏輯。

kit.name: 羅馬短劍
kit.history: 刺劍不是用來揮砍的。短兵相接靠的是盾的邊緣和刺突的節奏。

countries: 交戰的三方：其一是北歐維京船團——並非國家，而是以數十艘長船為核心、沒有後方的武裝群體，戰士多來自挪威西南岸、丹麥島嶼與法國西北部海岸，首領姓名在現存阿拉伯編年史中完全無存，補給靠沿途劫掠與登岸取糧，武器紀律卻極嚴。其二是科爾多瓦埃米爾國，也就是安達盧斯，執政者哈卡姆二世於961年至976年在位，名義上統有伊比利亞半島南部，軍權集中在他與宰相穆罕默德·伊本·阿巴德手中，並有常備艦隊與各城民兵。第三方是伊比利亞北部的基督教諸侯，以加利西亞與阿斯圖里亞斯王系的諸侯為代表，加上沿大西洋海岸的小型封建領地；這些勢力與埃米爾國彼此爭鬆，卻在外敵當前可以短暫合作。真正左右海上局面的力量仍在埃米爾國手中：859年埃米爾阿卜杜勒·拉赫曼二世曾以約一百艘船的艦隊追擊並全殲維京人，說明科爾多瓦的船塢與海軍傳統足以對付北歐快船。
countriesEn: Three parties were involved. The first was the Viking war-band: not a state at all but an armed grouping built around several dozen longships, with no rear area behind it, its warriors drawn from the coasts of south-west Norway, the Danish islands and north-western France; no name of any leader survives in the Arabic chronicles, supply was taken by raiding along the way and by fetching food from the shore, and yet the discipline of arms was strict. The second was the Emirate of Córdoba, that is al-Andalus, ruled by Hakam II from 961 to 976, nominally holding the southern half of the Iberian peninsula, with military power concentrated in his own hands and those of his vizier Muhammad ibn Abbad, supported by a standing fleet and by the militias of individual towns. The third were the Christian princes of northern Iberia, represented by the counts of Galicia and Asturias and by the small lordships along the Atlantic coast; these were permanently at odds with the emirate and squabbled among themselves, yet they could cooperate briefly when a common enemy appeared. The decisive weight of sea power, however, still lay with the emirate: in 859 Emir Abd al-Rahman II sent a fleet of roughly a hundred ships against the raiders and destroyed them, which shows that the Cordoban yards and naval tradition were quite capable of dealing with northern fast ships.
people: 維京方的首領在史料中查無實名，這本身就是一種資訊：十世紀的北歐劫掠船團常由數支部隊臨時拼湊而成，頭目推舉而非常設，名字隨船隊解散而消失，現存阿拉伯編年史只以「北歐人」或「羅斯人」稱呼他們。可以確定的有兩件事：一是他們是沿大西洋海岸一路南下的北歐戰士團體；二是戰後殘部多被法國西北部的諾曼人吸收，於十一世紀隨諾曼人渡海參加曼齊刻爾特（1038–1053）與西西里戰役，北歐的暴力由劫掠轉為征服。穆斯林方面的核心人物是科爾多瓦埃米爾哈卡姆二世（al-Hakam II，961–976年在位），他在位期間把中央控制延伸到安達盧斯最偏遠的西部，966年這場遠征迫使他同時徵召海軍與西部軍鎮的兵力；其宰相穆罕默德·伊本·阿巴德出身基督徒家庭、受過宮廷教育，掌文書與軍務。基督教方面幾乎沒有留下同期記載，可指名的只有加利西亞與阿斯圖里亞斯王系的諸侯，以及在868年前後由維馬拉·佩雷斯家族開啟、從安達盧斯手中逐步收復的北方據點。地方層面上，阿爾加維一帶的伊德里斯王朝後裔與柏柏爾系的 Banu Udhruh 勢力，是聯軍在地面上的支柱。
peopleEn: No name of any Viking leader survives in the sources, and that absence is itself a kind of information: tenth-century northern raiding crews were often thrown together from several bands, their chief chosen for the occasion rather than holding office, and his name disappeared with the dispersal of the fleet; the surviving Arabic chronicles call them only Normans or Rus. Only two things can be stated with confidence: first, that they were a war-band of northern warriors who had sailed south along the Atlantic coast; second, that the survivors were largely absorbed into the Norman group in north-western France and crossed the sea with the Normans in the eleventh century to take part in the campaigns at Mantua and in Sicily, so that northern violence turned from plunder into conquest. The central figure on the Muslim side was the Cordoban emir Hakam II (al-Hakam II, reigning 961–976), who during his reign extended central control into the far western districts of al-Andalus; the expedition of 966 forced him to mobilise the fleet and the garrisons of the western military districts at the same time. His vizier Muhammad ibn Abbad, born into a Christian family and educated at court, handled the chancery and much of the military administration. On the Christian side almost no contemporary account survives; the only figures one can name are the princes of the Galician and Asturian royal lines, together with the northern footholds that the family of Vimara Peres had begun to take back from al-Andalus around 868. At local level, the descendants of the Idrisid dynasty and the Berber group known as the Banu Udhruh around the Algarve were the local pillars of the allied army.
kits: 卡面這件兵器是羅馬短劍（gladius），一種約公元前五世紀定型、劍身狹長而近乎直刃、雙刃、護手呈圓盤狀的步兵佩劍；它在帝國後期因軍制改革與工藝過時而退出一線戰鬥，此後在歐洲留下兩種命運：一方面演成五至七世紀的遷移時期短劍，另一方面在伊比利亞的兵器譜系中留下一個「短身直刃」的類型，與後來的伊比利亞直刃軍刀共享形制邏輯。就966年這場戰役而言，這件兵器並不是維京人實際攜帶的型制——北歐戰士用的是更長、漸尖、帶圓頭護手的雙刃直劍，配長矛與丹麥斧；它也不是聯軍的制式裝備，安達盧斯步兵用「喬希爾」（jowshir）這類彎刃刀與「哈爾比」（harbi）長矛，北方基督徒用伊比利亞式直刃劍與刺盾。但就戰鬥邏輯而言，羅馬短劍所代表的那套方法仍然在場：短劍不是用來揮砍的，靠的是盾的邊緣與刺突的節奏，而這正是盾牆正面交鋒的核心。實際上雙方共有的裝備有：圓形盾牌（北歐用彩繪木盾，安達盧斯用蒙皮圓盾「迪爾斯」dirs 與小盾「圖爾斯」turs）、長矛、北歐的獵弓與安達盧斯的「卡瓦斯」（qaws），以及九至十世紀北歐已能取得並穿著的鎖子甲（mail hauberk，稱 gusa）。攻城器械方面，這場戰役沒有攻城記載：維京人不帶攻城塔與配重投石機，只靠突襲與破壞；聯軍同樣沒有投入大型圍城器械。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the Roman gladius, a legionary sword that took its settled form around the fifth century BC: a narrow, nearly straight, double-edged blade with a round disc-shaped guard. It fell out of first-line service in the later empire as military organisation and workmanship changed, and afterwards it had two lives in Europe: on one hand it turned into the short swords of the Migration Period in the fifth to seventh centuries, on the other it left behind a short straight-bladed type in the Iberian weapon lineage, sharing its formal logic with the later Iberian straight swords. For the campaign of 966 this weapon was not the type actually carried by the Vikings, who used longer, tapering double-edged straight swords with round pommels, together with spears and Danish axes; nor was it the standard equipment of the allied army, since Andalusi infantry carried curved blades such as the jowshir with harbi lances, while the northern Christians used Iberian straight swords and stabbing shields. In terms of combat logic, however, the method the gladius represents was still present: a short sword is not swung, it depends on the edge of the shield and on the rhythm of the thrust, and that is the core of a shield-wall engagement. The equipment actually shared by both sides included round shields (painted wooden shields for the north, the leather-covered dirs and the small turs of al-Andalus), spears, the hunting bow of the north and the qaws of al-Andalus, and the mail hauberk (called gusa), which the north could obtain and wear by the ninth and tenth centuries. As for siege equipment, this campaign left no record of any: the Vikings brought no siege towers and no counterweight trebuchets, relying on surprise and destruction, and the allies likewise committed no heavy siege ordnance.
tactics: 維京人的整套戰術是為「不佔地」而設計的：船隊沿大西洋海岸航行，在缺乏情報的岸點突然登岸，迅速掃掠鄉村與修道院，把可搬走的財物、牲畜與人丁裝船，然後在援軍抵達前轉移到下一處海灘；他們避免攻堅，所以不帶攻城塔與配重投石機，也不打正面會戰。844年圍塞維爾四十四日、以木製火攻與投射物逼退維京人的記錄，說明他們一旦被守軍拖住就必須撤退；859至861年在塔霍河口被安達盧斯海軍追擊全滅，說明其艦隊缺乏海上正面作戰能力。這一次他們又遇上同一道難題：登陸點在半島西南端的聖文森特海角，一端是大西洋、一端是開闊沙地，任何船隊都無法隱蔽接近，而聯軍由科爾多瓦沿海路推進、由艦隊封住退路，把北歐人限制在一小片海灘上。聯軍的做法是穆斯林與基督徒混合編隊：步兵以盾牆與長矛列陣，吸收北歐人的第一次衝鋒，輕騎與弓箭手從兩翼擾動，待北歐人登岸人數受限、陣形被拉開後再合圍衝擊，殘餘者被追擊清理到海上。史料沒有留下這場戰役的部署細節，以上是從安達盧斯海軍與前線軍鎮的一貫做法反推的合理輪廓。
tacticsEn: The whole Viking tactical system was designed for not holding ground. The fleet moved along the Atlantic coast, landed suddenly at points where it had no intelligence, swept through villages and monasteries with speed, loaded movable wealth, livestock and captives into the ships, and shifted on to the next beach before a relief force could arrive; they avoided sieges, so they brought no siege towers and no counterweight trebuchets and fought no set-piece battle. The record of the siege of Seville in 844, forty-four days long, ended by wooden fire devices and missiles, shows that once they were held up by a garrison they had to withdraw; the destruction of the raiders at the mouth of the Tagus in 859–861 by the Andalusi fleet shows that their ships were poor at fighting an enemy on the open sea. This time they ran into the same difficulty: the landing point lay at Cape St. Vincent at the south-western tip of the peninsula, with the Atlantic on one side and open sand on the other, so no fleet could approach unseen, while the allied army advanced along the coastal road from Córdoba and the fleet closed the sea route, pinning the northmen to a narrow stretch of beach. The allied method was mixed columns of Muslim and Christian troops: infantry closed up in a shield wall with spears to absorb the first charge, light horse and archers worked both flanks, and when the northmen's numbers ashore were limited and their formation had been stretched out, the allies counter-charged and encircled, driving the survivors into the sea. The sources do not preserve the deployment of this battle; the outline above is a reasonable reconstruction from the consistent practice of the Andalusi fleet and the frontier military districts.
data: 可以確定與只能推算的數字要分開。確定的是：年分，主流編年史記966年，部分記965年；戰役在科爾多瓦埃米爾哈卡姆二世（961–976年在位）任內；戰場在今葡萄牙阿爾加維的聖文森特海角一帶，該處坐標約為北緯37.0度、西經9.0度。距離上，聖文森特海角至里斯本約一百九十公里，至科爾多瓦直線約三百八十至四百公里，陸路約四百五十公里；從北歐人在法國大西洋沿岸的基地南下至此，沿岸航行須超過一千五百公里。推算：以長船每日八至十公里的沿岸航行速度，單程便要四個月上下，因此這類遠征只能利用春末至初秋的作戰季，季節性限於一年之中能承受的那一段。艦隊規模方面，現存編年史沒有為966年留下船數；可以拿844年的戰役作對照——當年阿拉伯史料只以「數十艘」形容北歐艦隊，而859年埃米爾國出動的追擊艦隊明記約一百艘，這個對比說明安達盧斯具備系統性建造與徵用戰艦的產能，北歐船團則靠志願者湊船，難以長時間維持遠征。傷亡數字沒有任何可信記載。
dataEn: Numbers that can be established and numbers that can only be estimated have to be kept apart. What is established: the year, given as 966 in the main chronicles and as 965 in some; the fact that the campaign took place under the Cordoban emir Hakam II (reigning 961–976); and the battlefield, in the region of Cape St. Vincent in the Algarve of modern Portugal, at roughly 37.0 degrees north and 9.0 degrees west. As for distances, Cape St. Vincent lies about a hundred and ninety kilometres from Lisbon and roughly three hundred and eighty to four hundred kilometres in a straight line from Córdoba, some four hundred and fifty kilometres by road; from the northern bases on the Atlantic coast of France the coastal passage southward runs to well over a thousand five hundred kilometres. By estimate: at a coastal speed of eight to ten kilometres a day for a longship, the outward passage alone takes something like four months, so an expedition of this kind could only use the campaigning season from late spring to early autumn, and the season constrained it to the one stretch of the year that could be borne. As for the size of the fleet, the surviving chronicles leave no ship count for 966; the siege of Seville in 844 provides a comparison, since the Arabic source there speaks only of several dozen northern ships, whereas the pursuing fleet sent out by the emirate in 859 is recorded as about a hundred ships. The contrast shows that al-Andalus possessed the capacity to build and levy warships systematically, whereas northern crews assembled ships out of volunteers and could not easily sustain a distant expedition. No reliable casualty figures survive.
cause: 為何會打起來，理由分三層。第一層是地緣：北歐劫掠集團在九世紀末失去了法國內陸的基地——萊茵與塞納河一帶的據點在919年前後被攻破，盧瓦爾河與南特一帶的北歐駐留點在930年代被法蘭克與布列塔尼的領主聯手掃清（具體年份各史料略有出入），於是這批人沿大西洋海岸南移尋找新的收入來源，而波利尼西亞與愛爾蘭已開發到收益遞減，剩下最富的目標就是安達盧斯與伊比利亞北部。第二層是經濟：科爾多瓦埃米爾國是西歐最富的稅收中心之一，教堂、修道院與城鎮裡存放大量金銀器皿、象牙、香料與奴隸，遠征一趟便足以資助整支船隊維持一整年。第三層是政治：安達盧斯與北方天主教諸侯長期爭奪邊境與改宗權，沿海各城守備薄弱、地方貴族彼此傾軋，給了北歐人情報與縱容的空間；而966年前後阿爾加維一帶的伊德里斯王朝後裔與柏柏爾部族處境不穩，哈卡姆二世正需要一次成功的鎮壓來證明中央的權力。於是這場戰爭並非有明確外交目標的遠征，而是一次由利益驅動、機會主義的劫掠，遇上了一次同樣想藉戰果鞏固權力的反擊。
causeEn: Why this came to blows can be read at three levels. The first is geography: the northern raiding groups lost their bases in the French interior towards the end of the ninth century. The strongholds in the Rhine and Seine areas were broken up around 919, and the northern footholds in the Loire and around Nantes were cleared in the 930s by Frankish and Breton lords acting together, though the sources differ slightly on the exact years. The men moved south along the Atlantic coast looking for new sources of income, and since the Baltic and Irish lands had been worked down to diminishing returns, the richest remaining target was al-Andalus and northern Iberia. The second level is economics: the Cordoban emirate was one of the wealthiest tax centres in western Europe, with stores of gold and silver plate, ivory, spices and slaves in its churches, monasteries and towns, so a single voyage could fund a crew for a full year. The third level is politics: al-Andalus and the northern Christian princes had long fought over the frontier and over the right of conversion, coastal towns were thinly garrisoned, and local nobles intrigued against one another, giving the northmen both information and room to operate; and around 966 the Idrisid descendants and the Berber tribes of the Algarve were unsettled, so Hakam II needed a successful show of force to demonstrate the authority of the centre. The war, in other words, was not a distant expedition with a defined diplomatic aim but an opportunistic raid driven by profit, which met a counter-stroke fought by men who wanted the same thing: a victory that would consolidate their own position.
impact: 短期看，這場戰役是北歐大西洋劫掠的最後一次大規模成功。966年之後，維京人再沒有組織起同等規模的遠征伊比利亞的船隊；原先在安達盧斯沿海作戰的北歐戰士轉而投向法國西北部的諾曼人集團，隨諾曼公爵的旗幟在十一世紀渡海參加曼齊刻爾特（1038–1053）與西西里戰役，歐洲的「北歐暴力」由劫掠轉為建國。伊比利亞的戰局也從此改變方向：南方失去了安達盧斯的有效屏障，十二世紀由教宗與卡斯提利亞王國支持的收復失地運動在1085年奪回托萊多，1100年代逼近里斯本，最終由阿方索·亨利克斯在1147年攻下里斯本，並在1189年由桑喬一世在阿爾莫哈德王朝的協助下攻取希拉斯（Silves），完成對阿爾加維的重新征服，穆民再次被逐出海岸。中期最重要的影響是政治象徵：這場戰鬥是伊比利亞有明確記載的、基督徒與穆斯林為對付共同外敵而短暫並肩的少數例子，它為其後的合作模式提供了先例——1111年葡萄牙王桑喬一世與阿爾莫拉維德首領優素福·伊本·塔什芬之間的和約與軍事合作，以及卡斯提利亞與阿爾莫拉維德的聯盟，都建立在同一種「外敵在前」的邏輯上。最後，它在記憶層面上把阿爾加維的基督徒海岸領主與北方王室的共同戰鬥經歷固定下來，這段共同的抗北歐記憶在後來收復阿爾加維的戰役中被反覆引用。
impactEn: In the short term this campaign was the last great large-scale success of the northern Atlantic raiders. After 966 no fleet of comparable size was ever organised again to raid Iberia; the northern warriors who had fought along the Andalusi coast turned instead to the Norman group in north-western France and crossed the sea with the Norman dukes in the eleventh century, taking part in the fighting at Mantua and in Sicily, so that the northern violence of Europe turned from plunder into state-building. The Iberian war map also changed direction: the south lost the effective shield of al-Andalus, the reconquista movement backed by the papacy and the crown of Castile took Toledo in 1085 and pressed towards Lisbon in the 1100s, and the coast was finally retaken: Lisbon in 1147 under Afonso Henriques, and Silves in 1189 under Sancho I with the help of the Almohads, which completed the reconquest of the Algarve and pushed the Muslim population back out of the littoral. The most important mid-term effect was symbolic. This was one of the few clearly documented instances in Iberia of Christians and Muslims standing shoulder to shoulder against a common enemy, and it set a precedent for the pattern of cooperation that followed: the treaty and the military partnership between King Sancho I of Portugal and the Almoravid leader Yusuf ibn Tashfin in 1111, and the alliance between Castile and the Almoravids, both rest on the same logic of an enemy in front. Finally, at the level of memory, the campaign fixed a shared experience of fighting between the Christian coastal lords of the Algarve and the northern royal houses, and that common memory of resisting the northmen was invoked repeatedly in the later campaigns to recover the Algarve.
result: 結果是北歐遠征的失敗與崩潰。維京船團在聖文森特海角被穆斯林與基督徒聯軍擊敗：登陸的一批被殺或被俘，餘眾退向船隊，退路被聯軍艦隊在海角附近截斷，極少數船隻得以北返歐洲。聯軍則取得一次可以向哈卡姆二世交代的勝利：西部軍鎮恢復對阿爾加維的控制，埃米爾國的軍威在西南邊境得到彰顯，北方諸侯也藉此確認自己可以與穆斯林並肩作戰，同時保住自己的地盤與信仰。從裝備與戰術角度看，這場戰役也留下了一個清楚的反證：北歐快船在陸上會戰不可靠，而安達盧斯倚仗海軍與道路的體系，可以在自己的海岸把北歐人拖進它擅長的環境。此後三百年，伊比利亞沿海再也沒有出現同類遠征，跨海而來的北方武裝改以領地征服與王朝移植的方式進入半島——先是十一世紀末登陸的諾曼人，隨後才是法蘭克—卡斯提利亞王朝從北方逐步南下的收復戰爭。
resultEn: The outcome was the failure and collapse of the northern expedition. The Viking crews were beaten at Cape St. Vincent by the allied Muslim and Christian army: those who had landed were killed or taken prisoner, the rest made for their ships, the sea route was cut off by the allied fleet near the cape, and only a very few vessels got back north to Europe. The allies in their turn won a victory they could report to Hakam II: the western military districts recovered control of the Algarve, the military prestige of the emirate was displayed on its south-western frontier, and the northern princes confirmed that they could fight beside the Muslims while keeping their own territory and their own faith. In terms of equipment and tactics the campaign also left a clear demonstration: northern fast ships were unreliable in a land battle, while al-Andalus, resting on a system of fleet and roads, could drag the northmen onto the ground where it was strong. For three centuries afterwards no comparable expedition appeared on the Iberian coast, and northern armed forces entering the peninsula across the sea did so instead through the conquest of territory and the transplant of dynasties — first the Normans who landed at the end of the eleventh century, and then the reconquest pressed steadily southward by the Frankish-Castilian dynasties.
